label: Vaguely
title_raw: なんとなく ([なんとなく] )(Vaguely)
title: なんとなく
meaning: Vaguely, somehow どことなくに通じる

examples.japanese: あの人はなんとなく母を想いださせる。
examples.body_text:
あの人はなんとなく母を想いださせる。 

		She 
		vaguely 
		resembles my mother.
examples.body_html:
あの人はなんとなく母を想いださせる。 
She vaguely resembles my mother.

examples.japanese: なんとなく京都に行きたくなった。
examples.body_text:
なんとなく京都に行きたくなった。 

Somehow 
		I wanted to go to Kyoto.
examples.body_html:
なんとなく京都に行きたくなった。 
Somehow I wanted to go to Kyoto.

comments.text: なんとなく and どことなく can be used interchangely in many cases. However, なんとなく refers to something that is vague and not capable of pinpointing when it deals with something more or less abstract, whereas どことなく refers to vagueness that deals more or less with physical subject matter.
comments.html: なんとなく and どことなく can be used interchangely in many cases. However, なんとなく refers to something that is vague and not capable of pinpointing when it deals with something more or less abstract, whereas どことなく refers to vagueness that deals more or less with physical subject matter.

comments.text: A Japanese friend once told me that you could use なんとなく by itself as a reply to a question you don't feel like answering or don't know how to answer specifically. Any native speakers care to agree/disagree with this?
